# Pulte Group (PHM) Deep Dive Analysis

Report 067 | Published 2021-09-19 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2021-9-19/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/067.json)

China contagion, uranium timing, and homebuilders.

Pulte was a strong selection and reached the illustrative 2023 price level, despite a mistaken rate-suppression premise. The bank analysis underestimated duration and funding risk. China contrarian confidence remained weakly supported; explicit uncertainty around SP 500 avoids an artificial directional score. Uranium premium timing requires the actual daily trigger history, separate from eventual commodity upside.

**Coverage:** Read blocks 0-231 and 37 image labels. Covers macro/sovereign risks, crypto outages, uranium premium conditions, detailed PHM/DHI housing-credit thesis, valuation scenarios and execution risks. Personal travel anecdotes and routine holdings excluded.

Defaulted principal is not necessarily a 100% loss: recovery, collateral and provisions matter. Under zero recovery, 10% loss on 83% of assets indeed equals 8.3% of assets; without that assumption the claimed capital wipeout overstates the loss.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Evaluate the explanation separately from subsequent price direction.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Deductive assessment:**

- Risky assets 83% of total
- 10% default share
- Loss given default LGD
- Capital8.3% of total

Loss/assets=.83*.10*LGD=.083*LGD; all capital lost only if LGD=1 before offsets.
